conventions.convention: The factor count is an integer k ≥ 1; runs are all sign vectors in {−1,+1}^[k]. Columns are indexed by subsets A, with x_A the product of coordinates in A and x_∅ = 1. Row and column orderings are arbitrary but fixed.
The normalized coefficient is 2^(−k) times the signed response sum. For nonempty A, the factorial effect is the mean over x_A = +1 minus the mean over x_A = −1.

Replication is the same integer r ≥ 1 at every run. All run-replicate errors are mutually independent real random variables on one probability space, have finite second moments, and have common finite variance σ². Zero means and Gaussian laws are not assumed.
The effect estimate uses equally weighted run averages, and the effect-to-coefficient factor of two applies only to nonempty subsets.

load_bearing.statement: For integer k ≥ 1, the full run set is {−1,+1}^[k]; X has entries X_(x,A) = x_A = ∏_(j∈A) x_j, with x_∅ = 1. The normalized coefficient is 2^(−k)∑_x x_A y_x; for nonempty A, the factorial effect is the positive-sign group mean minus the negative-sign group mean.
For the full factorial design, ⟨c_A,c_B⟩ equals 2^k when A = B and zero otherwise. Thus XᵀX = 2^k I and 2^(−k)XᵀX = I. This is a deterministic property of the design matrix.

Under the stated fixed-coefficient model with equal replication r, mutually independent errors with finite second moments and common variance σ², Var(β̂_A) = σ²/(r2^k) for every A. For nonempty A, τ̂_A = 2β̂_A and Var(τ̂_A) = 4σ²/(r2^k). Zero error means are not required for these variance identities.

published_dependencies.used_for: The exact zero-inner-product criterion used in the orthogonality theorem and unequal-replication example.
The real coordinate pairing as a sum of coordinatewise products.
The measurable real-random-variable convention and the signed-error transformation in the variance proof.
Independence through generated sigma-algebras; deterministic sign changes preserve those sigma-algebras.
Expectation and finite-moment interpretation in the variance proof.
Variance and covariance definitions for square-integrable real random variables.
Covariance bilinearity and the variance scaling rules used for signed errors, coefficient contrasts, and factorial effects.
Variance addition for the finite family of signed independent errors.
